analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials yday risk Europe 3 Nov 2026
key_insights: Desk says S&P futures are slightly lower ahead of the US midterms, crude is bouncing after a sharp sell-off the prior day, and jobs data is due later in the morning.
KOSPI fell 359bps overnight and the desk noted a lack of AI sponsorship in the rally. Europe was more red than green, with France down 75bps.

Commodities: WTI is at $97 (up 100bps) and Brent at $106, off recent extremes but still elevated. Silver is down 3% and gold down 1%, back toward $3,900. The 10-year yield is 4.91%, DXY is $102 and Bitcoin is $77k.

Desk sees the prior day's strength in housing, autos, aerospace and airlines as coming from under-owned or shorted areas. It cautions the rotation could continue, with underperformance in AI/data center, distributors, chemicals and defensives.
ISM rose sequentially with new orders holding in the mid 50s. The desk expects PMI-levered names that have underperformed year to date on fears of 'peak' to rebound toward 60 into year end.
Privo says it is hard to separate fundamental from technical drivers. The market is nervous about the midterms, energy and rates, and investors are playing defense to protect first-half gains.
Privo notes the S&P has been higher in the 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950, and that gridlock has generally been supportive. AI and data center restrictions remain a risk.
Privo says index-related hedging was heavy on Friday. Sentiment and positioning have come down meaningfully, and clearing the event risk should be positive over time.

Privo's sequence of risks: avoiding an extreme midterm outcome (Texas is key), then whether the Middle East moves toward progress or re-escalation, then whether lower oil can deliver sustained relief in rates.

Q3 prints: ALSN beat and raised FY adj EBITDA and revenue guidance. CE beat on EPS and adj EBITDA but missed on revenue, and guided FY EPS above consensus. HUN missed on EPS but beat on revenue and adj EBITDA, with 4Q adj EBITDA guidance below consensus at the midpoint.
VVX beat on revenue and EPS and raised FY EPS and sales guidance, with book to bill of about 1.2x. BWXT beat on EPS and adj EBITDA but missed on revenue and narrowed FY EPS guidance.
CC missed on adj EPS and guided Q4 revenue far below consensus. CBT beat 4Q but guided 2027 EPS below consensus. HLMN was in line on EPS, beat on adj EBITDA and lowered FY revenue guidance.

Europe: GEBN SW was down 3% on in-line sales and a small EBITDA beat with guidance unchanged. SHAO GR was down 3% on a sales pre-release and a cost-cutting program. CLN SW was flat on a Q3 miss in Catalyst with full-year guidance unchanged.
AAPL was down 3% pre-market. Pre-market reports to watch: APTV, BALL, DD, ETN, EXPD, LDOS, LPX, RRX, ZBRA.

earnings_insights: ALSN Q3 reported EPS $2.90 vs consensus $2.32. Revenue $1.53bn vs consensus $1.47bn. EBITDA $400mn vs consensus $385.2mn. Guidance raised for FY adj EBITDA to $1.53-$1.58bn (prior $1.465-$1.575bn) and revenue to $5.975-$6.075bn (prior $5.8-$6bn). Net income guidance narrowed to $645-$685mn (prior $600-$700mn).

CE Q3 reported EPS $1.65 vs consensus $1.56. Revenue $2.56bn vs consensus $2.62bn. Adj EBITDA $548mn vs consensus $534.1mn. FY EPS guide $6-$6.25 vs consensus $6.02, FCF guide $750-$800mn, and year-end net debt to operating EBITDA of about 4.7x.

HUN Q3 reported EPS $0.04 vs consensus $0.07. Revenue $1.72bn vs consensus $1.61bn. Adj EBITDA $132mn vs consensus $119.7mn. 4Q adj EBITDA guide of about $60-80mn vs consensus $72.9mn. Net debt leverage expected to fall to about 4x by year-end.

VVX 3Q reported revenue $1.27bn vs consensus $1.22bn and EPS $1.64 vs consensus $1.50. Backlog was $12.8bn (funded $2.6bn) as of 2-Oct, with book to bill of about 1.2x. FY EPS guide raised to $6.15-$6.55 (prior $5.90-$6.30, consensus $5.94). FY sales guide raised to $4.95-$5.1bn (prior $4.875-$5.02bn, consensus $4.976bn).

CC 3Q adj EPS $0.21 vs consensus $0.27. Sales $1.54bn vs consensus $1.53bn. Adj EBITDA $200mn vs consensus $193.3mn. Q4 revenue guided to decline versus consensus of +6.5% y/y (the source text for the guided range is garbled). Q4 adj EBITDA guide $160-$185mn vs consensus $178.6mn, and capex guide $75-$85mn vs consensus $98.3mn. FY revenue growth guided to about 2% vs consensus +1.8%, and top end of FY adj EBITDA guide lowered to $775-$800mn (prior $775-$825mn).

BWXT 3Q adj EPS $1.26 vs consensus $1.18. Revenue $953mn vs consensus $976.1mn. Adj EBITDA $179.7mn vs consensus $168.8mn. FY adj EPS guide narrowed to $4.72-$4.77 (prior $4.70-$4.80), and FY adj EBITDA guided to $667mn (prior $662-$672mn).
CBT 4Q adj EPS $1.61 vs consensus $1.55. Net sales and operating revenue $1.01bn vs consensus $927.4mn. 2027 EPS guide $6.15-$6.75 vs consensus $7.01.

HLMN Q3 EPS $0.22 vs consensus $0.21. Revenue $457.5mn vs consensus $462.1mn. Adj EBITDA $90.2mn vs consensus $84.5mn. FY revenue guide lowered to $1.66-$1.68bn (prior $1.67-$1.72bn, consensus $1.68bn). FY adj EBITDA guide of about $285mn reaffirmed vs consensus $282.3mn.
GEBN SW was down 3% on in-line sales and a small EBITDA beat. Guidance unchanged, with a large acceleration in organic sales in the Americas and price cost pinching margins.
SHAO GR was down 3% on a sales pre-release and a cost-cutting program announcement. CLN SW was flat on a Q3 miss in Catalyst with full-year guidance unchanged.
Reports due 11/3 pre-market: AME APTV BALL BETA DD ETN EXPD GPK JBTM KNF LDOS LGIH LPX RRX WLFC ZBRA. The desk is focused on APTV BALL DD ETN EXPD LDOS LPX RRX ZBRA.
